item.description:

item.title: Lindsay Clancy was failed by our warped understanding of motherhood | Moira Donegan
item.description:
One of the things that I find very interesting about the Lindsay Clancy case is that it’s a complex fact pattern. There’s a fake thing that happens in psychiatry in which it’s assumed that people are capable of pure, easy diagnoses and that drugs are extremely effective. Neither one is true. If you spend any time with psychiatrists or with the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) — or people who have dealt with psychiatrists, the DSM, or medication — you would know it’s probably the least-developed area of all medicine. Psychiatry is incredibly vague. Basically, these things are diagnosed based on checklists and a person’s self-reported symptoms. And then when it comes to psychiatric drugs, very often it’s basically trying different combinations. It is virtually that basic: see what works, then adjust medication based on the symptoms. It’s really complex. In this…

item.title: Nepal holds a day of mourning as rescuers continue search for flood missing
item.description:
Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal. The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel. Continue reading...

Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24, The Guardian

item.title: Falling ceiling debris at Kennedy Center may mire debate over renovations
item.description:
The Kennedy Center shared photos on Saturday that showed a partial ceiling collapse that happened during a rainstorm in the main hallway of the over 50-year-old performing arts building. Roma Daravi, vice president of public relations for the Kennedy Center, said the collapse underscored the need to close the building for renovations. "Another example of the urgent need to close for renovation and revitalization, as our Chairman President [Donald] Trump has championed," Daravi said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital, adding, "This structural failure stems from decades of neglect and deferred maintenance by the previous leadership, and there’s no justification for further delays in restoring America’s cultural center." item.title: The White House Made an Arcade Game Out of Deporting People
item.description:
As of September 3, the official White House website features a page titled “arcade,” where users can play games like Rio Run, in which the player—a pixelated, white, and balding Border Patrol agent—collects “border crossers” and adds them to a line of orange-jumpsuited figures trailing behind him. It’s a retro-cutesy version of the nightmarish and very real scenes of ICE agents forcing immigrants, chained in a line, onto deportation planes. Other games in the “arcade” include Build the Wall, a Tetris rip-off in which the user builds a wall to “protect the border from the coming horde.” (Tetris, in response to Build the Wall, has posted on Instagram that the company takes copyright infringement “very seriously.”) There’s also an eagle-themed game called Flappy Bill, and a MAHA-oriented school lunch game. It’s no surprise, considering the “wartime recruitment” framing of ICE’s current…

Sources: ABC News, Aftermath, Mother Jones
